title: How to Hack Your Brown Fat for Better Health
description: There’s a special type of fat in your body that burns calories like a literal furnace. A major new study , published just a few days ago, now links it to better cardiovascular health, metabolic health, and even mental health. It’s called brown fat. And there are at least 4 different ways to turn it on. In fact, I’ve used one of these myself to burn over 600 more Calories per day without any change in activity, drawing on insights from another randomized controlled trial I’m going to tell you about later. But first, let’s review these new data and what they really mean. Oh, wait! One more teaser before we begin. In case you’ve already seen the headlines around this paper, I promise I have some extra nuances for you, including a paradox buried in the paper itself that hasn’t been discussed. Once I show it to you, I think you’ll understand why I find it particularly interesting. But I’m getting ahead of myself. Let’s understand what makes brown fat special, and the describe the headline findings. What Makes Brown Fat Special? Most of the fat on your body is white fat. White fat is like your lazy friend who walks 2,000 steps a day and hates exercise, whereas you, my brown bestie (okay, that didn’t come out right), are a ball of endless energy! But in all seriousness, brown fat is built differently. Brown fat cells are crammed with mitochondria, which give the tissue its brownish tint because mitochondria are packed with iron. And those mitochondria are the literal engines of your cells. However, they don’t just generate energy for your muscles to use; they also generate heat energy through a different pathway that runs through something called uncoupling proteins (UCP), in particular UCP1.

title: This Saturated Fat Slows Heart Disease
description: Foods I eat almost every day contain a saturated fat that new research suggests can prevent heart disease. Yes, you heard that right. A saturated fat. So yes, technically speaking, it is very fair to say that “This saturated fat slows heart disease.” We will review the preclinical data, as well as data in humans showing its relevance. But that’s not even close to the weirdest part of this story. This is a paper that was almost an exercise to read, as I had to keep lifting my jaw up off the floor. I learned crazy facts about the microbiome, caffeine, and statins. And over the next few minutes, I want to try to confer that scientific awe to you, along with some practical insights. But let’s begin where this study began, with a group of healthy individuals and a group of individuals with heart disease. The Bacterium That Fights Heart Disease The researchers set out to investigate the role of the gut microbiome in cardiovascular disease. So, they took 223 healthy people and 189 with cardiovascular disease and looked at which bacteria differed among them. Four of the dominant species belonged to the genus Bacteroides , and the standout was one called Bacteroides uniformis (B. uniformis) , which was linked to cardiovascular health in humans. That’s just an association, however. So, they took a group of healthy teenagers, wiped out their microbiomes with powerful antibiotics, and gave half a microbiome transplant enriched in Bacteroides uniformis , and have a control microbiome transplant. Then, they followed them for 30 years. Just joking. Ya… we can’t do that, practically or ethically. But the joke has a purpose: to make the point that when we have interesting associations like this we need to turn to animal models to flesh out mechanisms and cause-effect relationships.

title: Could You Live to 200? (Lessons From a Whale)
description: What if one of the greatest secrets extending human life has been hiding inside the largest animals on Earth? It’s the bowhead whale. These creatures can live 250 years, which means there are bowheads around today that were born before the light bulb was invented. They can weigh more than 200,000 pounds, and have mouths large enough to fit an entire SUV. But I’m not telling you about this extraordinary creature simply because of its immense size or incredible longevity. I’m telling you about it because of a biological paradox that may help explain how it lives so long. Something you’ve probably never thought about. Something we could use. These whales should be riddled with tumors. But they aren’t. Think about it. Every time a cell divides, it has to copy its DNA. And every time DNA is copied, there’s a chance of making a mistake that could ultimately lead to cancer. Now consider that this whale has roughly a 1000-times more cells than a human, and some those cells divide for centuries. More cells. More cell divisions. More opportunities for cancer-causing mutations. These whales should be swimming tumors! And yet, they appear remarkably resistant to cancer. So what’s their secret? And more importantly, could we harness that secret to protect ourselves from cancer, and even extend human lifespans far beyond what we currently imagine possible? Scientists are beginning to think we might.
